package_info.why_malicious: These versions of Moq introduced a closed-source, obfuscated sub-dependency (Devlooped.SponsorLink) that, without user consent, reads the developer's local git config to extract their email address, hashes it, and sends it to a remote server controlled by the package author. This constitutes unauthorized data exfiltration and a privacy violation.

execution_context.trigger: build-time (during application build or CI/CD pipeline)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Process.Start('git', 'config --get user.email'); // then hash and send to remote server
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code spawns an external git process to read the user's email from the global git config, hashes the email, and sends the result to hxxps://cdn.devlooped[.]com/sponsorlink via HTTPS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it collects personally identifiable information (PII) from the developer's environment and exfiltrates it to a third-party server without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build-time dependencies should not access user configuration files or exfiltrate any data. Legitimate packages do not read or transmit developer PII during build or install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or licensing systems may collect environment data, but only with clear user consent and transparent documentation.
key_indicators: Obfuscated, closed-source DLL included as a dependency
Spawning external git process to read user email
Hashing and exfiltrating data to a remote server

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code checks for specific environment variables and evades execution if they are present, attempting to avoid detection or opt-out scenarios.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Evasive behavior to avoid execution in certain environments is a common anti-analysis technique in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate telemetry or licensing code should provide clear, documented opt-out mechanisms, not hidden or undocumented environment variable checks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise software may use environment variables for feature toggling, but this should be documented.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code downloads additional configuration from a remote server, potentially allowing dynamic modification of telemetry or exfiltration behavior.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading remote configuration at build-time allows the author to change behavior without user knowledge, increasing risk.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build-time dependencies should not fetch remote configuration unless clearly documented and consented to.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software updates configuration from a server, but this is typically transparent and documented.

attack_chain.action: User installs or builds a project with Moq 4.20.0/4.20.1, pulling in Devlooped.SponsorLink as a dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of SponsorLink code during build.

attack_chain.action: SponsorLink code executes at build-time, checks for environment variables to determine if telemetry should be disabled.
attack_chain.leads_to: If not disabled, proceeds to collect user data.

attack_chain.action: SponsorLink code spawns a git process to read the user's email from git config.
SponsorLink code hashes the email and sends it to hxxps://cdn.devlooped[.]com/sponsorlink.
attack_chain.leads_to: User data is exfiltrated to a remote server.

attack_chain.action: SponsorLink code may download additional settings from hxxps://cdn.devlooped[.]com/sponsorlink/settings.ini to modify behavior.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential for dynamic changes in telemetry or exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Spawning external git processes to read user config
Hashing and exfiltrating developer email addresses
file_indicators: Presence of Devlooped.SponsorLink.dll in dependency tree
Obfuscated, closed-source DLLs in NuGet packages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build and CI/CD environments for unexpected execution of external processes (e.g., git config), especially from obfuscated or closed-source DLLs. Flag any outbound network connections to cdn.devlooped.com during build or install phases. Audit dependency trees for the presence of Devlooped.SponsorLink or similar closed-source, obfuscated packages. Alert on any build-time access to user configuration files or exfiltration of hashed email addresses.
